newsitem.title: UK: BP says UK Sullom Voe to handle Schiehallion crude.
newsitem.headline: BP says UK Sullom Voe to handle Schiehallion crude.

text.p: British Petroleum said on Friday it intended to award to Sullom Voe oil terminal on Scotland's Shetland island a contract to handle production from BP's new Schiehallion oilfield.

Subject to final negotiations, Sullom Voe would enter an agreement with BP on behalf of the Schiehallion co-venturers Amerada Hess, BP Murphy, OMV, Shell and Statoil for a minimum period of five years, BP said.

"This is an important award which provides the Schiehallion co-venturers with a reliable shipment route and also provides Sullom Voe with additional volumes and income," said Greg Bourne, Director BP Scotland.
Sullom Voe already handles output from the multi-field Brent blend stream.
Oil from Schiehallion, expected to run at 140,000 barrels a day (bpd) after first oil in mid-1998, will be handled separately from Brent, a BP spokesman said.
Four storage tanks at the terminal will be refurbished and Sullom Voe's jetty number three recommissioned.
The award comes as good news for Sullom Voe which only last summer secured its future by clinching a new deal with the 28 oil companies which use it to export Brent.

"Not only will the local economy see immediate benefits from the 10 million pound investment required to handle Schiehallion exports, but we can now look forward to the future with even greater confidence," said Terry Kirchin, manager of the terminal.
Sullom Voe lost out to the Flotta terminal in the Orkney islands for the contract to handle production from BP's Atlantic Foinaven field which comes onstream this year.
BP said crude from the 400 million barrel Schiehallion field will be exported to Sullom Voe by a new purpose built shuttle tanker operated by the company.
Shipping company AP Moller are having the 125,000 tonne tanker built by Daewoo in Korea and will lease the vessel to BP.
